Technology stocks were ending in a deep hole Monday, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing almost 3.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was dropping over 4.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) EchoStar ( SATS ) after the satellite services company's Hughes Network Systems segment Monday announced three African telecom companies have selected its Hughes Jupiter system to deliver satellite broadband services for their customers. Terms of the individual contracts with Botswana Telecommunications Corp, Satcom Networks Africa Limited (SatCoNet) and an unnamed telecommunications firm in eastern Africa were not disclosed.
In other sector news:
(+) Apptio ( APTI ) jumped over 52% on Monday after agreeing to an all-cash $1.94 billion going-private transaction led by an affiliate of Vista Equity Partners. Under terms of the proposed offer, Vista will pay $38 for each Apptio share, representing a 53% premium to Friday's closing price. Apptio, which helps customers manage, plan and optimize their investments, also has a 30-day "go-shop" to actively solicit and potentially enter negotiations for alternative buyout proposals.
(+) Black Box ( BBOX ) raced over 29% on Monday after accepting a buyout proposal from AGC Networks Pte Ltd, the Singaporean subsidiary of AGC Networks Ltd that will soon launch a $1.08-a-share tender offering for the IT infrastructure company. After completing the tender offer, AGC Networks plans on acquiring all remaining Black Box shares not tendered for $1.08 per share through a second-step merger.
(-) SAP ( SAP ) declined as much as 6% on Monday after the German software giant said it was acquiring all outstanding shares of Qualtrics International for almost $8 billion in cash. The purchase price includes unvested employee incentive compensation and cash on the balance sheet at the close. SAP said it is expecting the acquisition will help bolster its experience management offering and help customers to better manage supply chains, networks, employees and core processes.
